claims.statement: The review pooled two myeloma prophylaxis studies comparing LMWH with aspirin. Symptomatic VTE RR .51 (CI .22 to1.17), sparse bleeding and secondary comparisons remain uncertain; the direction is LMWH relative to aspirin. This does not establish aspirin efficacy versus no prophylaxis, firm superiority/equivalence, absence of harms or tumor benefit.

The same Palumbo trial supplied the fixed low-dose warfarin/aspirin comparison: VTE RR1.50 (CI .74 to3.04) with sparse bleeding and other endpoints. These shared arms are not independent patients or proof of equivalent PE prevention.

The review describes one VTE in the aspirin group and none on rivaroxaban in a23-person conference-abstract pilot, with no major bleeds reported in either group. Explicit outcome-arm denominators and precise follow-up are unavailable here; no rate, superiority or general safety conclusion is established.

sourceQualifications.description: Newly diagnosed myeloma with specific lenalidomide/thalidomide regimens, no prior VTE in the two main studies and selected antithrombotic eligibility. Does not automatically apply to other modern regimens, established VTE treatment, every myeloma patient or anticancer efficacy. Background anticoagulant effects across other cancer types are CONTEXT only.

Review-reported open-label designs; Palumbo high attrition/selective-reporting risk, Larocca high performance/detection risk, Campos-Cabrera all unclear. Source-reported formal GRADE is not a new independent site grade. Lack of I2 heterogeneity with two sparse studies does not remove bias/imprecision.

Review cutoff3August2020 is historical, not our comprehensive current search. WHO ICTRP August2020 entry says portal unavailable; some printed query year restrictions end2019 despite2020 headings. What's New says six new ongoing studies while main results/flow say five new reports; retain source reporting discrepancy. Protocol differences include added fatalPE/Tau2 and analyses not performed. No fresh external correction/retraction or registry check.

Review support lists no direct Italy/Netherlands funding and Scottish Chief Scientist Office support for editorial base. MDN declares consultancy fees; others none. Constituent trial product support/conflicts are secondhand. No no-conflict inference from funding alone.
